data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Vitamins & trace elements_

**Class:** Fat-soluble vitamin (retinol and its esters)

## Mechanism of action
- Needed for epithelial differentiation, vision (rhodopsin), immunity; precursor of retinoic acid

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Vitamin A deficiency: phrynoderma (follicular hyperkeratosis), xerosis, night blindness, xerophthalmia, Bitot spots
- Measles in children (reduces mortality), prophylaxis in national programme (6–59 months)
- High-dose vitamin A was once used for acne, Darier disease and PRP (replaced by retinoids)

## Dose & formulations
- National prophylaxis: 1 lakh IU at 9 months, then 2 lakh IU every 6 months up to 5 years
- Xerophthalmia/measles: 2 lakh IU on days 1, 2 and 14 (half dose under 1 year)

## Adverse effects
- Acute toxicity: raised intracranial pressure (bulging fontanelle, headache, vomiting), desquamation
- Chronic hypervitaminosis A: dry skin, cheilitis, alopecia, bone pain, hepatotoxicity, hypercalcaemia
- Teratogenic in high doses

## Contraindications
- High doses in pregnancy (>10,000 IU/day); with oral retinoids

## Drug interactions
- Oral retinoids (additive toxicity); orlistat and mineral oil reduce absorption

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid doses above 10,000 IU/day (teratogenic).

## Viva points
- Phrynoderma — toad skin of vitamin A deficiency
- Never give vitamin A supplements with isotretinoin/acitretin

_Sources: Khopkar (Vitamin A — retinol); Wolverton 4e ch.40. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
